title: Parkinson's disease: stages over years
description: Parkinson's disease develops over many years, so this timeline is in stages of the disease, not minutes. Its core is the loss of dopamine-producing cells in a small midbrain structure, the substantia nigra, which leaves the striatum, part of the movement system, short of dopamine. Unlike most other states in the app, the dimming in the substantia nigra and striatum here stands for that loss of dopamine cells and their nerve endings, as seen on tracer scans, not for lower activity. The disease also affects many other parts of the nervous system.
caveat: The stages are assembled from separate kinds of evidence: post-mortem studies of where the disease's protein deposits are found, tracer scans that measure dopamine nerve endings, and brain scans of activity at rest. These were never one experiment, and the stages are built from people at different points of the disease, not by following individuals. The earliest changes, in the lower brainstem and the smell pathway, come from post-mortem staging of protein deposits; they are described here but not drawn, because they are deposits, not a measured change in activity. Pooled analyses of activity at rest describe the results of earlier studies as inconsistent. How fast the disease moves, and which symptoms come first, varies a great deal between people.

phases.name: Before movement symptoms
phases.caption: In post-mortem studies the disease's protein deposits are first found low in the brainstem and in the smell pathway, and climb upward from there. This stage is described, not drawn: those are deposits seen under the microscope, not activity.

phases.name: Dopamine cells are lost
phases.caption: Dopamine-producing cells in the substantia nigra are lost, and the striatum runs short of dopamine. Tracer scans show the loss is greatest at the back of the putamen, with the caudate relatively spared. Movement becomes slower and stiffer.

order.rationale: The post-mortem staging places the midbrain after the lower brainstem. That this precedes the movement symptoms in each person is not measured in the sources read; the order follows the staging.

phases.name: Movement circuits change
phases.caption: With less dopamine, the circuits the striatum belongs to change their activity. In pooled scans at rest, the lentiform nucleus, which includes the putamen, and the thalamus are among the regions whose activity is lower than in people without the disease.

order.rationale: The resting-state findings come from people at varied stages and are compared with healthy people, not followed over time. Placing them after the dopamine loss is an inference from the dopamine loss being the cause.

phases.name: Changes widen
phases.caption: Later, the protein deposits reach the cortex, starting in the temporal lobe and then frontal and association areas, and many symptoms beyond movement can appear. Researchers also link the cerebellum to the disease. These are described, not drawn, because the sources read give no direction of activity for them.

order.rationale: From post-mortem staging of protein deposits, not from activity measured over time.

regions.explanation: Loss of the dopamine-producing cells here is one of the defining features of Parkinson's disease. The dimming stands for that cell loss, not for measured activity. How much is lost before symptoms appear is not given in the sources read, so the level drawn is illustrative.

citations.authors: Poewe W, Seppi K, Tanner CM, Halliday GM, Brundin P, Volkmann J, Schrag AE, Lang AE
citations.title: Parkinson disease.
citations.quote: Neuronal loss in the substantia nigra, which causes striatal dopamine deficiency, and intracellular inclusions containing aggregates of α-synuclein are the neuropathological hallmarks of Parkinson disease.

regions.explanation: Dopamine nerve endings are markedly reduced here in people with Parkinson's disease, in a pooled analysis of tracer scans, and the back of the putamen is the most affected part of the striatum. The dimming stands for that loss, not for activity. The whole putamen is drawn; the loss is greatest towards the back.
